MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Medical Scientist - Microbiology Laboratory Pool





Job no: 945128

Work type: Full time, Part time

Located in: Various

Categories: Science, Engineering, Technical




 
Central Adelaide Local Health Network

Statewide - SA 

Various Locations

Salary: MeS-1 $73,533 - $89,764 p.a. (pro-rata) + Superannuation & Salary Sacrifice Benefits

Various - full time, part time, ongoing and temporary contracts will be available through the pool.

About the role

Join our Microbiology team as a Medical Scientist (MeS-1) and begin an exciting career journey in a dynamic diagnostic laboratory environment. This role provides the opportunity to apply your scientific knowledge and technical skills while contributing to the delivery of accurate, reliable and high-quality pathology services that support patient care. Under appropriate guidance and supervision, you will perform a range of routine microbiology diagnostic techniques, participate in the testing process from planning through to reporting, and develop your expertise in laboratory practices, quality processes and scientific methodologies.

As an important member of our multidisciplinary team, you will work alongside experienced scientists, technical staff and medical professionals to support the delivery of exceptional laboratory services. You will have opportunities to build your professional capability through competency-based training, contribute to teaching and research activities, and assist with the development and implementation of new techniques and approaches. This role offers a supportive environment where you can grow your skills, strengthen your professional judgement and progress your career within medical science.

About you

You are an enthusiastic and dedicated Medical Scientist with a passion for diagnostic microbiology and a commitment to delivering accurate, high-quality pathology services. You will bring a strong foundation in laboratory science, a willingness to learn and develop your skills, and a collaborative approach to supporting a positive and professional team environment.

Qualified and developing scientist - You hold an appropriate Medical Science qualification recognised under NPAAC requirements and have an understanding of diagnostic microbiology, infectious diseases and general pathology laboratory practices.

Quality focused and technically capable - You have the ability to perform routine diagnostic testing, follow laboratory procedures, operate and troubleshoot equipment, apply scientific principles and contribute to the delivery of accurate and reliable results.

Organised and proactive team member - You can prioritise workloads, manage time effectively, work with increasing independence, identify potential issues and use initiative while contributing positively within a multidisciplinary laboratory team.

Effective communicator with a commitment to service - You demonstrate strong communication skills, maintain confidentiality, provide professional customer service and build positive working relationships with scientific, technical and clinical colleagues.

About us

Statewide Clinical Support Services (SCSS) is a unique public healthcare organisation that serves health consumers and provides specialist clinical services to the health system in South Australia. SCSS encompasses BreastScreen SA, SA Dental, SA Medical Imaging, SA Pathology, and SA Pharmacy. Come and work with us to improve the health and well-being of South Australians, across all age groups and at any time of their life or health need. 

What we offer

Salary Benefits: Enjoy flexible salary packaging options, including up to $9,010 each FBT year for living expenses (such as mortgage, rent, utilities and groceries) plus an additional $2,650 for meal and entertainment expenses.

Professional Development: Opportunity to apply for reimbursement of eligible professional development activities, and access to dedicated leave for ongoing learning.

Annual Leave: Enjoy paid recreation leave for essential rejuvenation, with leave loading applied.

Health and Fitness Benefits: Access to Fitness Passport, a discounted workplace health and fitness program for you and your family, plus an annual voluntary flu vaccination to support your wellbeing.

Employee Assistance Program: Confidential counselling and support services for you and your family via our Employee Assistance Program.

Diversity and inclusion:

Statewide supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe at work. The culture aims to encourage all people to use their talents and to be valued and rewarded for their contributions.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants are encouraged to apply. 

Application Information:

Please refer to the role description for essential educational-vocational qualifications that may be required.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and compliant Immunisation screening as indicated in the role description.

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.

Please note that unsolicited applications from recruitment agencies or third parties will not be accepted for this position.

Malissa Amato,

Workshop Planner for Construction Machinery Manufacturers   
  Workshop Planner  
 Location: Revesby, NSW Pay Rate: $50 per hour + super Duration: 6-month contract (full-time hours) with potential to go permanent 
   
  The Opportunity  
 A well-established construction machinery manufacturing company in Revesby is seeking a Workshop Planner to join their on-site operations. This is a hands-on planning and coordination role responsible for scheduling machinery through the workshop, managing subcontractors, and ensuring all Australian compliance checks are completed. 
 You'll play a key part in keeping large and heavy construction machinery moving through the workshop efficiently-balancing planning, procurement, communication, and technical understanding. This is a 6-month temporary role with strong potential to transition into a permanent position for the right candidate. 
  Key Responsibilities  
 
 Plan and coordinate machinery workflow through the workshop 
 Ensure machinery meets relevant Australian standards and compliance requirements 
 Manage subcontractors and ensure timely delivery of services 
 Oversee movement, purchasing, and procurement of parts for heavy machinery 
 Maintain schedules, track progress, and adjust plans as needed 
 Liaise with workshop teams, engineers, and operations staff 
 Identify bottlenecks and propose practical, outside-the-box solutions 
 Use Microsoft Projects and internal systems to manage timelines and tasks 
 
  About You  
 
 Experience in a workshop, automotive, truck, heavy machinery, or construction environment 
 Background in planning or scheduling, ideally with machinery or vehicles 
 Strong technical understanding; mechanical engineering experience desirable 
 Process-driven mindset with strong organisational skills 
 Confident communicator with the ability to influence and coordinate across teams 
 Creative problem solver able to think outside the box 
 Comfortable using Microsoft Projects or similar tools (training provided) 
 
  Requirements  
 
 Relevant trade or engineering exposure (mechanical, automotive, fabrication, or workshop) 
 Experience with scheduling tools such as Microsoft Projects 
 Full working rights in Australia 
 On-site availability in Revesby 
 
  Why Apply?  
 
 Competitive rate: $50 per hour + super 
 6-month contract with strong potential for permanency 
 Work with a respected construction machinery manufacturer 
 Hands-on role with training provided 
 Supportive workshop and engineering team 
 Opportunity to step into a long-term career pathway 
 
 
 
  Apply Now  
 
 
 If you're a workshop or engineering professional with planning experience and ready for your next opportunity, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today or email cathal.maguire@hays.com.au.  Please  click here  to apply.
